title: The Call He Kept Postponing

protagonist.name: Subir Lahiri
protagonist.coreConflict: The habit of treating time as an elastic, forgiving currency that can always be settled next weekend.

counterpart.name: Niladri Sen
counterpart.role: Fabrication engineer, Jamshedpur; college friend from Presidency (1996–1999)
counterpart.dynamic: The friend who kept reaching across geography and routine with short, persistent invitations that required only fifteen minutes to answer.

setting.primary: Prince Anwar Shah Road flat, South Kolkata
setting.secondary: The suburban local train to Jamshedpur via Kharagpur; the Telco colony verandah
setting.atmosphere: Grey monsoon afternoons, flickering handset screens, unread notifications accumulating beneath spreadsheets

signatureObjects: The pocket diary with Niladri's original Jamshedpur landline number (0657) written in fading violet Quink ink
The 90-second voicemail left on October 14th: 'Subir-da, no disaster. Just watching the mist on the river. Pick up when you breathe.'
The two brass railway keychains bought together at Kharagpur junction in June 1998
structuralMilestones: The notification deferred during an audit meeting on a Tuesday afternoon
The accumulation of missed calls across six years masquerading as harmless delay
The sudden call from Niladri's younger sister at 6:40 AM on a Saturday
The four-hour train journey where Subir reads back through their silent digital thread
The arrival at the silent Telco colony house and the conversation that can never happen
